# Choosing a filter or a transition

Drawn from each pack's `SKILL.md`: its Role, what it suits and doesn't (the first sentence of each point) and how long it holds up. Choose here, then read the pack's own guide for the settings and the setting that mends a picture it fails on.

## Print

| Filter | Role | Suits | Doesn't suit | How long |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/cmyk` | Structure: it remakes the picture as print, keeping its colours. A finish may go over it. | Saturated, colourful pictures: every colour survives as its dots (checked on a coloured-light portrait and a product set). · Mid-key and bright pictures; black type from 40 px prints solid. | Dark pictures: the worst case of all the filters here, almost nothing of a low-key portrait is left. · A white page of interface: the screen has little to print and chews the small text. · Text under 40 px, and coloured text of any size. | An accent: 1–3 seconds, the moment something is "in print". Never a long stretch, never over a shot whose information must be read. |
| `emile/halftone` | Structure: it remakes the picture. Colour under it is lost; a finish (grain) may go over it. | Portraits lit from one side and products on a plain ground: the shape survives as dots (checked on a mid-key and a coloured-light portrait and a product set). · Bold type from 48 px up: black type prints solid and stays crisp. · amount 0.5 lays the dots over the picture in its own colours: a softer, printed-colour look. | Dark pictures: most of the frame prints solid and the subject is lost (a low-key portrait, a night set). · Text in a mid-tone or a colour, and any text under 32 px: it breaks into dots. · More than about five seconds at a time: it tires the eye. | An accent: one moment of 1–4 seconds (a line, a poster held still), five seconds at most for a section. Never over a shot whose information must be read (an interface, numbers, body text). |
| `emile/risograph` | Structure: it remakes the picture in two inks. Nothing goes under it but the picture; a finish is not needed (it brings its own sand and paper). | A warm subject on a cool or plain ground: they separate into the two inks (a face in the second ink, its backdrop in the first; checked on a mid-key and a coloured-light portrait). · A product's screen: type stays readable, the accent colour goes to one ink. · grain 0.4–0.7 for the sandy screen, misregister 0.2–0.5. | Dark pictures: two inks overprinted only reach a dark plum, so a low-key frame turns to one murky field (checked on a low-key portrait; no setting mends it). · A picture all in one hue (a blue lake printed in blue and red is just blue). · Colours that must be exact (a brand colour, a product's colour): every colour becomes a mix of the two inks. | Mostly an accent: a title card, a chapter card, the end card, 2–5 seconds. A whole opening (about ten seconds) only when the brand itself is independent and hand-made. |

## Texture

| Filter | Role | Suits | Doesn't suit | How long |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/dither` | Structure: it remakes the picture in two colours. Nothing over it: a finish would blur the pixels. | Portraits and products in mid-key or bright light (checked: the face holds in both patterns). · Headlines: black type stays solid. · Held shots and slow moves. | Low-key pictures: the darks fall into solid ink (a low-key portrait keeps little). · Text in a mid-tone, and small text. · Fast or textured motion: the pattern stays still while the picture moves under it, and it crawls. · Long stretches. | An accent: 1–4 seconds, the moment we see as the machine does; it only works between clean shots. Never a long stretch. |
| `emile/grain` | Finish: the last filter on top, over colour and structure. | Every kind of picture checked (products by day and by night, portraits, a landscape): the picture is never lost under it. · Flat, drawn or rendered clips that look too smooth. | Small text and fine interface at amount above 0.3: the grain sits in the letters. · Footage that is already noisy. · A bright, crisp, high-tech look. | A finish, so it may run long: at amount 0.25 or under it can cover the whole film and give footage from different sources one surface. Heavier (0.4 and up) only for one moody section. |
| `emile/paper` | Finish: on top, over colour. Not with halftone, risograph or cmyk: they bring their own paper. | Light pages, illustrations and flat graphics: the tooth shows best on light, even areas. · Type of any size: the texture doesn't break letters. | Dark scenes: the sheet can't be seen under dark ink, and the blacks only go grey. · Photographs and footage meant to look real: the tooth reads as dirt on the lens. | A finish, so it may run long: an illustrated explainer or words on a page can take it for a section or the whole film (texture 0.5 or under). Never on live footage or product shots. |

## Distort

| Filter | Role | Suits | Doesn't suit | How long |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/displace` | Optics: over the picture and its colour, under a finish. | Portraits, products and type alike: the picture stays whole under it (checked on every kind of picture). · Short spans, two seconds or less, placed on a beat. | Long spans: it tires and stops meaning anything. · Calm, trust and reassurance (money, health, safety). · Words that must be read during the hit: a slipped band cuts through letters. | An accent: 0.3–1.5 seconds, on the beat or the moment something goes wrong. Past two seconds it means nothing. |
| `emile/fluted-glass` | Optics: over the picture and its colour, under a finish. A filter clip changes every track under it, so type that must be read goes on a track above the clip. | Portraits: a face stays a face behind the ribs (checked on three portraits). · Products, gradients and colourful footage; shapes wider than about three ribs. · amount under 1 is thinner glass (less bend and frost), not a mix of two pictures. | Anything that must be read: letters double behind the ribs (a product's screen turns unreadable). · Thin lines and small interface: they break up. | An accent: 1–3 seconds before a reveal, or a ground for one line of large type. Never over information that must be read; words go on a track above the filter. |

## Color

| Filter | Role | Suits | Doesn't suit | How long |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/duotone` | Colour: under structure and finish. | Every kind of picture checked, low-key ones included: the safest filter here. · Pairs that work: navy #0e1a33 with bone #f3ead9 (default); oxblood #3a0a12 with cream #f6e7d8; forest #0b2e2a with butter #f2e8cf; near-black #05070d with ember #ff6a2b for night. | Pictures where colour carries meaning: a chart with coloured series, a product in several colours, red and green for bad and good. · A whole long film: the eye stops seeing it. | A section: one shot to one scene (a memory, an emphasis, a ground for words). The whole film only to pull mixed sources into the brand's two colours, and only when asked. |
| `emile/palette` | Colour that also simplifies shape: under structure and finish. | Portraits and products in mid-key or bright light: a face becomes four or five flat shapes and stays a face (checked on two portraits). · A product's screen: it stays readable, its colours snap to the palette. | Dark pictures at the defaults: everything falls into the darkest ink (a low-key portrait, a night set). · Noisy footage: the edges speckle. · Colours that must be exact. | An accent: 2–5 seconds, one designed moment; thermal can carry a whole shot about seeing what is hidden. Never the whole film. |

## Glow

| Filter | Role | Suits | Doesn't suit | How long |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/bloom` | Optics: over the picture and its colour, under a finish. Grain over it suits it. | Dark pictures with bright points: white type, small lights, thin bright lines, highlights on dark products (checked on a night set and a dark panel). | Bright pictures: nothing happens (checked: a bright product set and a white page of interface come out unchanged). · A wide, soft glow that fills the frame: the radius stops at about 2% of the frame's short side, because a filter draws in one pass. · Fine detail one or two pixels wide looked at closely: its glow is a little uneven. | As long as the shot: the dark shot with points of light, for its whole length. It is restrained and hides nothing. |

## Film

| Filter | Role | Suits | Doesn't suit | How long |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/chromatic-aberration` | Optics: over the picture and its colour, under a finish. | lens: every kind of picture checked; the centre is untouched, so a face or a product in the middle stays sharp. · shift: bold shapes and big type for a short hit. | shift over words that must be read: letters triple. · shift for a whole scene: it stops being a moment. · lens at high strength on an interface with small text near the corners. | lens at a low strength may follow a whole shot, or the whole film, to give rendered pictures a lens. shift is a hit of 0.3–1 second only. |
| `emile/crt` | Medium: the last thing before a finish; it shows whatever is under it on a tube. | Every kind of picture checked: dark and saturated ones best. · amount under 1 is a flatter, cleaner tube (less bulge, fainter lines). | Small text: 24 px type softens between the lines. · Fine detail that must stay crisp (a product beauty shot). · Films that will be watched very small: the phosphor stripes can shimmer when the player scales them. | A section: the "back then" part, 2–6 seconds, or one screen inside the frame. Never the whole film. |
| `emile/vhs` | Medium: the last thing before a finish; it shows whatever is under it as a tape. | Footage and portraits; saturated colours (the bleed shows on them) and dark scenes (the snow shows in them). | Small text: everything softens sideways, body text under 28 px blurs. · A crisp interface demo or a product beauty shot. · The whole of a film that isn't about the past. | A section: the memory or the old footage, 2–6 seconds, then a cut back to the clean present. The whole film only when the whole film is about the past. |

## Transitions

| Transition | Length | Suits | Doesn't suit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `emile/dissolve` | 0.3–0.8 s | A change of scene with nothing to lead the eye from one to the other. · Calm films, talk, a pause between chapters. | Fast cuts on a beat: it reads as hesitation. · Two pictures with text in the same place: the words overlap half way. |
| `emile/push` | 0.3–0.6 s | A change of scene that goes forward in a story or a process. · A swipe-like feel for mobile and product films. | Going back to an earlier scene: the direction says "next". · Pictures with fine detail at the edges, which smears on a fast push. |
| `emile/wipe` | 0.3–0.6 s | Lists, steps and comparisons: one thing after the next. · Explainers and product films with a flat, designed look. | Soft, painterly looks (ink, watercolour): the straight edge breaks them. · A presenter in the middle of the frame: the edge crosses the face. |
| `emile/zoom` | 0.4–0.8 s | From an overview into one part of it. · Energetic openings and reveals. | Text-heavy pictures: the type blurs as it scales. · Several in a row: it tires the eye quickly. |
